title: Driver Lets Go of Wheel in New Truck
main_content:
The first self-driving truck began its first trip on a major European highway last week.

The German automobile company Daimler made the vehicle, which is named Actros. It is perhaps the first mass-produced truck whose driver will only be required to watch the vehicle’s movements. The driver will have duties similar to those of an airline pilot while the plane flies in autopilot mode.

Wolfgang Bernhard, the head of Daimler’s trucks and buses division, drove the Actros.

The Actros reached a speed of 80 kilometers an hour while driving down the busy road.

Radar, a number of video cameras and sensing devices watch other vehicles and road conditions. The truck will ask the driver to take control of the vehicle in dangerous situations. If the driver does not, the truck will slow to a stop by itself.

Daimler says its trucks will help drivers on long road trips and in stop-and-go traffic conditions. The company hopes governments will pass laws to permit the use of its self-driving trucks by 2020.

What will the truck do in dangerous situations?
options: Take control away from the driver
Ask the driver to take control or stop
questions.answer: Ask the driver to take control or stop
